title: Portable generator service handoff
description: A populated project inside the existing application. It uses the same 30-stage project state, records, runs, evidence, defect, regression, baseline and release model as ordinary projects. It is not the application itself.

userEnteredData.exactRequest: Create a phone-readable service handoff for portable generator GEN-042. Record completed service work and checks, preserve unresolved safety facts as UNKNOWN, block return-to-service when a safety-critical condition is unresolved, and include the escalation path required by the supplied site policy.
userEnteredData.requestedDeliverable: One Markdown handoff artifact for the field technician.
constraints: Use only ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or BLOCKED for release

objective.exactUserObjective: Create a phone-readable service handoff for portable generator GEN-042 that records completed work, preserves unresolved safety facts correctly, enforces the safety gate, and includes the site-policy escalation path.

sourceInventory.title: SITE_POLICY.md
sourceInventory.relevantPortions: required handoff content, safety gate, escalation

researchRecords.finding: Exact objective, deliverable, unit identifier, no-invention rule, safety-unknown handling, and escalation requirement extracted.
Required service content, safety gate, and escalation sequence extracted.
Conflict/exception/prohibition pass completed; no new material requirement category found.

requirements.requirement: The handoff must preserve the exact customer objective and identify the requested deliverable.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Objective and deliverable are present without changing their meaning.
requirements.failureCondition: Objective or deliverable is omitted or materially changed.

requirements.requirement: The handoff must record the unit identifier, service date, completed service actions, functional start/stop check, and exterior leak inspection.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: All required handoff elements are present.
requirements.failureCondition: Any required handoff element is absent.

requirements.requirement: An unresolved safety-critical condition must be represented as UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and must prevent a ready-for-service claim.
requirements.applicability: When a safety-critical fact is unresolved
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: The output blocks return-to-service and does not convert missing evidence into success.
requirements.failureCondition: Ready-for-service is asserted while a safety-critical condition is unresolved.

requirements.requirement: The final handoff must include an escalation path for a found or unresolved safety-critical condition.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Escalation states stop, record blocker, identify missing evidence/repair, route for resolution, then revalidate.
requirements.failureCondition: Escalation is absent or does not preserve the stop-and-revalidate sequence.

requirements.requirement: Release must be ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or BLOCKED according to affirmative evidence and unresolved mandatory conditions.
requirements.observableSatisfactionCondition: Exactly one allowed release state is recorded and supported by evidence.
requirements.failureCondition: A fourth state is used or acceptance lacks affirmative evidence.

tests.procedure: Compare the project objective and requested deliverable to REQUEST.md.
tests.failureCondition: Objective or deliverable is omitted or materially changed.

tests.procedure: Check that every required service-handoff element appears in the final artifact.
tests.failureCondition: Any required handoff element is absent.

tests.procedure: Evaluate the safety-gate logic against an unresolved-condition fixture.
tests.failureCondition: Ready-for-service is asserted while a safety-critical condition is unresolved.

tests.procedure: Compare escalation wording to the required stop → blocker → resolution → revalidation semantics.
tests.failureCondition: Escalation is absent or semantically incomplete.

tests.procedure: Reconcile the release state against mandatory requirement evidence.
tests.failureCondition: A fourth release state is used or acceptance lacks affirmative evidence.

mutations.violationMode: Set ready-for-service while a safety-critical condition remains UNKNOWN.
Use PROVISIONALLY ACCEPTED as a release state.

productionInstruction.objective: Produce the phone-readable GEN-042 service handoff from the authorized project sources.
productionInstruction.sourceAuthority: User request controls the requested result; site policy controls service-handoff and safety semantics; workflow rules control outcome vocabulary.
procedure: Preserve the exact project objective and unit/date context.
Record each completed service action and required check from authorized evidence.
Represent unresolved facts as UNKNOWN; if a safety-critical fact is unresolved, create a blocker and do not claim ready-for-service.
Include the site-policy escalation sequence: stop, record blocker, identify missing evidence or repair, route for authorized resolution, then revalidate.
Use exactly one release state from ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or BLOCKED and state supporting evidence.
productionInstruction.completionCriteria: REQ-001 through REQ-005 are SATISFIED with preserved verification evidence.

generatedPrompts.title: Initialize the job
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 01: preserve the exact GEN-042 request, deliverable, supplied materials, constraints, assumptions, unknowns, and input-set identity.

generatedPrompts.title: Build source inventory
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 02: inspect REQUEST.md, SITE_POLICY.md, and WORKFLOW_RULES.md; record authority, relevance, versions, conflicts, and inspection state.

generatedPrompts.title: Research requirements
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 03: research each authorized source, extract obligations, prohibitions, exceptions, dependencies, applicability, and repeat until no new material category appears.

generatedPrompts.title: Compile requirements
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 04: convert candidate obligations into atomic requirements with stable IDs, traceability, observable satisfaction, verification method, failure condition, and severity.

generatedPrompts.title: Resolve requirement set
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 05: check duplicates, conflicts, impossible combinations, undefined terms, circular dependencies, prerequisites, unsupported requirements, applicability, and verification paths.

generatedPrompts.title: Build verification suite
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 06: create one verification procedure for every mandatory requirement before production instruction authoring; prefer deterministic methods when applicable.

generatedPrompts.title: Build failure tests
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 07: create invalid fixtures for realistic violation modes and verify validators reject or block them as required.

generatedPrompts.title: Author production instruction
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 08: author the GEN-042 production instruction from the resolved requirements, including safety branches, output contract, failure behavior, and completion criteria.

generatedPrompts.title: Preflight instruction
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 09: independently preflight the instruction for ambiguity, missing information, conflicts, unavailable capabilities, unverifiable commands, ordering, failure behavior, and traceability.

generatedPrompts.title: Freeze candidate
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 10: freeze the exact candidate versions, identities, hashes where practical, tool configuration, and distribution rules for the iteration.

generatedPrompts.title: Run ten executions
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 11: run ten fresh isolated executions of the frozen GEN-042 candidate; no run may see another run output or reviewer feedback; preserve every output separately.

generatedPrompts.title: Verify runs
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 12: independently verify every active requirement for each of ten runs and record SATISFIED, VIOLATED, or UNDETERMINED with evidence.

generatedPrompts.title: Compare runs
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 13: compare all ten verified runs without selecting a favorite; preserve repeated failures, unique failures, variance, and inconclusive verification.

generatedPrompts.title: Root cause defects
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 14: trace every material defect backward to the earliest defective layer rather than patching only the visible symptom.

generatedPrompts.title: Create regression tests
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 15: convert each confirmed defect into a permanent regression that fails before correction and succeeds afterward.

generatedPrompts.title: Revise responsible layer
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 16: correct the earliest responsible layer, create controlled identities for changed artifacts, and invalidate all affected downstream determinations.

generatedPrompts.title: Rerun iteration
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 17: freeze the corrected candidate and run ten new fresh executions; repeat verification, comparison, root cause, regression, and correction.

generatedPrompts.title: Convergence
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 18: calculate exact convergence metrics and require 100% coverage/regression success with zero critical or major defects, mandatory unknowns, contradictions, ambiguities, or unexplained variance.

generatedPrompts.title: Unchanged confirmation
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 19: run ten new independent contexts with absolutely no candidate change and verify the converged result remains stable.

generatedPrompts.title: Freeze baseline
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 20: freeze the unchanged-confirmed production baseline with exact approved component identities and immutable file hashes.

generatedPrompts.title: Generate product
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 21: in a fresh production context generate the actual GEN-042 handoff from the approved baseline only and preserve the output identity.

generatedPrompts.title: Deterministic product verification
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 22: run every applicable deterministic test against the actual finished GEN-042 artifact bytes and reject any mandatory failure.

generatedPrompts.title: Semantic verification
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 23: independently compare the finished handoff meaning against semantic requirements and authoritative source evidence.

generatedPrompts.title: Adversarial verification
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 24: attempt to disprove the finished handoff, including omissions, false-ready claims, unsupported release state, wrong versions, terminology drift, unhandled cases, and regressions.

generatedPrompts.title: Representation inspection
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 25: inspect the exact delivered Markdown representation, file integrity, section order, missing content, and transformation/package defects.

generatedPrompts.title: Reconcile process and product
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 26: establish process correctness and product correctness separately, then reconcile them without using either as proof of the other.

generatedPrompts.title: Release gate
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 27: apply exactly one release state—ACCEPTED, REJECTED, or BLOCKED—from affirmative requirement and validator evidence.

generatedPrompts.title: Verify artifact identity
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 28: recalculate SHA-256 for the exact selected release artifact and authorize only a byte-identical audited-hash match.

generatedPrompts.title: Preserve evidence chain
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 29: preserve source → requirement → instruction → execution → product → test → result → evidence → release links for every mandatory requirement.

generatedPrompts.title: Preserve failures
generatedPrompts.prompt: Stage 30: preserve every defect and permanent regression so a reappearing failure remains reproducible and release-blocking.

stageEvidence: STAGE 01: Captured the exact GEN-042 request, deliverable, three supplied sources, constraints, assumptions=NONE, and the initially missing service date blocker; INPUT-v002 records the resolved date.
STAGE 02: Inventoried REQUEST.md, SITE_POLICY.md, and WORKFLOW_RULES.md; no unresolved controlling conflict remains.
STAGE 03: Completed source-by-source research and a second exception/prohibition pass; extracted five material obligations.
STAGE 04: Compiled five atomic mandatory requirements with stable IDs, applicability, evidence, verification methods, failure conditions, and severity.

STAGE 05: Checked every requirement-set defect class; no unresolved duplicate, conflict, impossible combination, undefined term, dependency, support, applicability, or verification-path defect remains.
STAGE 06: Built one verification procedure per mandatory requirement; mandatory test coverage is 5/5 = 100%.
STAGE 07: Built four invalid fixtures and confirmed the assigned validators reject or block them as required.
STAGE 08: Authored the production instruction from REQUIREMENTS-v001 with objective, inputs, authority, scope, ordered procedure, safety branch, output contract, and completion criteria.
STAGE 09: Independent preflight identified the missing escalation output requirement; after correction, INSTRUCTION-v002 has no unresolved material preflight defect.
STAGE 10: Froze CANDIDATE-001 with exact source, requirement, test, instruction, and tool identities.
STAGE 11: Executed ten fresh isolated runs; each initial run omitted the escalation section and every output was preserved separately.
STAGE 12: Independently verified 5 requirements × 10 runs = 50 mandatory records; REQ-004 was VIOLATED in all ten initial runs.
STAGE 13: Compared all ten runs without selecting a favorite; the escalation omission was repeated across the batch.
STAGE 14: Root cause identified at the instruction layer: INSTRUCTION-v001 did not carry REQ-004 into the output contract.
STAGE 15: Created REG-001; the no-escalation fixture fails before correction and succeeds after correction.
STAGE 16: Created INSTRUCTION-v002 and invalidated downstream freeze, execution, verification, and comparison determinations.
STAGE 17: Froze CANDIDATE-002 and executed ten new fresh runs; all five mandatory requirements were SATISFIED in every run.

STAGE 18: Convergence reached 100% requirement coverage, 100% verification coverage, 100% regression success, and zero critical/major defects, mandatory unknowns, contradictions, ambiguities, or unexplained variance.
STAGE 19: Ran ten new unchanged confirmation contexts against CANDIDATE-002; identities were unchanged and all mandatory results remained SATISFIED.
STAGE 20: Frozen BASELINE-001 from the unchanged confirmed candidate.
STAGE 21: Generated the finished GEN-042 handoff from BASELINE-001 in a fresh production context.
STAGE 22: Ran deterministic structural and release-state verification against the actual finished artifact; all applicable deterministic tests SATISFIED.
STAGE 23: Independent semantic verification confirmed escalation and safety-gate meaning against authoritative sources.
STAGE 24: Adversarial review attempted omission, false-ready, unsupported-release, terminology-drift, and regression attacks; no unresolved critical or major defect remained.
STAGE 25: Inspected the exact Markdown delivery representation for missing sections, ordering, text loss, and file integrity; representation SATISFIED.
STAGE 26: Process correctness and product correctness were established separately and reconciled; both SATISFIED.
STAGE 27: Applied ACCEPTED because all five mandatory requirements have affirmative evidence and all mandatory validators succeeded.
STAGE 28: Rehashed the exact release artifact; audited SHA-256 and release SHA-256 are identical.
STAGE 29: Preserved complete source → requirement → instruction → execution → product → test → evidence → release links for all five mandatory requirements.
STAGE 30: Preserved DEFECT-001 and REG-001 permanently; the applicable regression succeeds for the approved baseline.
